title: New evidence for an accepted risk
question: A newly observed exposed service contradicts the owner’s control assumption. Which risk decision must be reopened, and why does a monitoring observation not itself accept the residual risk?
scenario: The risk owner accepted a customer portal’s residual risk on the recorded assumption that its administration service was unreachable from the internet. Monitoring now records inbound connections to that service, and vulnerability management confirms an exploitable version. No owner has reviewed the changed exposure.
focalRelation: Monitoring and vulnerability status provide evidence to risk management; the changed risk scenario then informs control selection. Evidence can reopen the decision, but only the accountable owner can accept residual risk.

nodes.label: Recorded risk decision
nodes.detail: The owner accepted residual risk only under the stated assumption that the administration service was not internet reachable.

nodes.label: Observed exposure
nodes.detail: Correlated telemetry shows unsolicited internet connections reaching the administration service; this is evidence about exposure, not a risk-acceptance act.

nodes.label: Exploitable version confirmed
nodes.detail: Vulnerability assessment confirms that the exposed service version has a relevant exploitable weakness.

nodes.label: Reopen scenario and controls
nodes.detail: Reassess likelihood, impact, control effectiveness, and treatment because a material assumption has changed.

nodes.label: Owner chooses treatment
nodes.detail: The accountable owner selects mitigation, avoidance, transfer, or documented acceptance after reviewing the updated residual exposure.

edges.label: assumption contradicted; prior decision no longer sufficient
updated risk scenario informs control and treatment choice

lanes.label: Operational evidence
lanes.rule: Observations can change confidence and assumptions but cannot exercise owner authority.

lanes.label: Accountable risk decision
lanes.rule: The owner reviews the updated scenario and records treatment and residual-risk authority.

states.title: The original decision has a condition
states.caption: Keep the reachability assumption attached to the acceptance; acceptance is not timeless.

states.title: Two observations contradict that condition
states.caption: Monitoring establishes reachability and vulnerability management establishes relevant exploitability. Neither observation is an acceptance decision.

states.title: Reassessment is required
states.caption: Reopen the specific scenario and control assumptions before choosing treatment.

states.title: Authority remains with the owner
states.caption: The owner records a treatment and any newly accepted residual risk after the reassessment.

variants.label: Compensating control also failed
variants.changedFact: The service was intentionally reachable, but the rate-limiting control used in the acceptance record is now disabled.

states.title: Control behavior changed
states.caption: Monitoring evidence contradicts the control-effectiveness assumption rather than the reachability assumption.

states.title: Reassess the same accountable decision
states.caption: The owner must review the updated residual exposure; the monitoring team still cannot accept it.

nodes.detail: Operational evidence contradicts the control-effectiveness premise of the acceptance.

nodes.label: Reassess control effectiveness and residual risk
nodes.detail: Recompute exposure and select treatment because the relied-on control behavior changed.

prediction.prompt: What should happen immediately after the exposed vulnerable service is confirmed?

options.label: Treat the alert as acceptance of the new residual risk
options.feedback: An observation has no risk-acceptance authority. It supplies evidence that reopens the owner’s decision.

options.label: Close the alert because the service was previously accepted
options.feedback: The acceptance depended on a reachability assumption that current evidence contradicts.

options.label: Reopen the risk scenario and route it to the owner
options.feedback: Correct. Two evidence sources contradict the accepted scenario, so reassessment and an accountable treatment decision are required.

prediction.hint: Separate the evidence-producing roles from the role authorized to choose treatment.

transfer.prompt: In the changed case, monitoring shows the accepted rate limit is disabled even though reachability was expected. What must be reconsidered?

options.label: The control-effectiveness and residual-risk assumptions
options.feedback: Correct. The changed control behavior alters the risk basis and informs a new control or treatment decision.

options.label: Only the telemetry retention period
options.feedback: Retention may matter to evidence quality, but the decisive change is that an accepted control assumption no longer holds.

options.label: Nothing, because the owner already accepted the service
options.feedback: Acceptance does not survive a material change to the scenario or assumed control effectiveness without review.

transfer.hint: Ask which fact the earlier decision relied on and whether that fact remains true.

retry.prompt: A third alert names the administration service as internet exposed, but independent validation proves the observed address belongs to an unrelated decoy and the service remains private. What follows?

options.label: Require the owner to accept a new internet-exposure risk despite the disproved correlation
options.feedback: The validated facts do not contradict the recorded reachability assumption, so there is no new exposure scenario to accept.

options.label: Correct the evidence record and preserve the existing decision unless other material facts changed
options.feedback: Correct. Monitoring evidence must be validated; a disproved correlation does not itself reopen or replace the owner’s decision.

options.label: Let the monitoring team record residual-risk acceptance because it investigated the alert
options.feedback: Investigation can establish facts, but it does not transfer risk-acceptance authority to the monitoring team.

retry.hint: First decide whether validated evidence actually changed the scenario; then keep authority separate from observation.

takeaway: Operational evidence can invalidate the assumptions behind a risk decision. It triggers reassessment and informs control selection; it does not itself accept residual risk.
assumptions: The original acceptance and its reachability assumption are documented.
The monitoring observation and vulnerability match the same service and time window.
The case does not assert exploitation; it establishes changed exposure requiring review.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The case makes all three assigned directed relationships learner-operable: two evidence streams reopen risk, and the updated risk scenario informs a distinct control/treatment decision.

learningJob.plainExplanation: reachability and exploitability evidence contradict the condition behind the existing acceptance, so the scenario and control assumptions must be reopened for an accountable owner decision. Monitoring supplies evidence but has no authority to accept residual risk.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: The revealed visual adds provenance from two observations into reassessment and then owner treatment, but the opening exposes only the prior decision record, so the initial figure carries almost none of the contradiction the prompt asks the learner to predict.
